Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with h/o type 1 diabetes, with recent 
admission for DKA, returns several days later for hypoglycemia, 
hypothermia, and altered mental status 

# Altered mental status:  Likely secondary to hypoglycemia.  
Head CT negative.  Tox screen negative for illicit substances.  
___ had BS 40 per EMS.  Patient denies taking more insulin than 
she should have.  She has however not been eating on a regular 
schedule.  The patient was discharged the day prior to admission 
after being hospitalized for DKA.  Consulted ___ for help 
with diabetes management.  ___ felt that Humalog ___ was 
not going to be a good choice for her because she does not 
comply with a regular diet.  She was started on Lantus insulin 
so that she would have some control although not optimal.  The 
patient was given insulin via sliding scale in the hospital.  
She is not compliant enough to use a sliding scale at home so 
she will be instructed to take 4 units humalog with every meal.  
She will follow up with ___ as an outpatient.

# Acute Anemia:  The patient's hematocrit was 34.1 at admission. 
 It then dropped to mid ___ and fluctuated at that range for the 
remainder of the admission, not requiring any transfusions.  
(Her Hct has been in high ___ most reccently.)  The 
patient denied any GI bleeding or back pain.  Hemolysis labs 
were unremarkable.  Stools were guaiac not checked as pt had not 
passed any stool while hospitalized. 

# Hypothermia, hypotension- Symptoms quickly resolved and were 
thought to be due to hypoglycemia as no sign of infection/sepsis 
(UA, CXR, BCx, WBC, TSH, Cortisol all negative or normal). 

# DM1 - Blood sugars remainded labile fluctuating between 400s 
and ___. She was followed by ___, who made adjustments in her 
basal and sliding scale insulin. 

# Coag negative staph bacteremia, line associated)  The patient 
was discharged to complete a 14 day course of vancomycin with 
___.

# AMS - Based on timing and quick resolution, most likely also 
due to hypoglycemia. 

# CAD:  History of prior NSTEMI in setting of cocaine and DKA. 
Pt was continued on Aspirin, Lisinopril, Toprol, Statin 

# Acute renal failure: Improved quickly with fluids, thought to 
be preranl. 

# Chronic pain:  Continue home regimen of 
Hydrocodone-Acetaminophen, gabapentin

# Anxiety:  Continue home benzo regimen

# GERD:  Stable.  Continue PPI.

# Phantom pain: Continue home percocet

# Peripheral Vascular disease, complicated by dry gangrene. Will 
need outpatient follow up with vascular surgery

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with altered mental status.  Evaluate for
acute process.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained through the brain.  No
contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of acute intra- or extra-axial hemorrhage,
edema, mass effect or major vascular territory infarction.  There is no
hydrocephalus.  The gray-white matter differentiation is preserved. There is a
small hypodensity in the left basal ganglia, likely a remote lacunar infarct.
Given the patients age, there is greater than expected prominence of the
ventricles and sulci, which is consistent with diffuse parenchymal volume
loss. The visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are well aerated.
No osseous abnormality is detected.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No acute intracranial abnormality.

2.  Greater than expected global atrophy for patients age. Clinical
correlation recommended.

INDICATION:  ___ female with altered mental status.  Evaluate for
acute process.

COMPARISON:  ___.

SINGLE UPRIGHT AP VIEW OF THE CHEST:  The lungs are clear without focal
consolidation, pneumothorax or pleural effusion.  The cardiomediastinal
silhouette and hilar contours are normal.  There is a right internal jugular
catheter which terminates over the cavoatrial junction without significant
change in the position compared to the prior study.  Osseous structures are
grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of acute intrathoracic abnormality.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with new hypoglycemia.

Comparison is made to the prior study of ___.

Findings: The right IJ distal tip projects in the cavoatrial junction.  The
heart size is mildly enlarged.  Specifically, the right heart border is more
prominent. The lungs are clear with no focal consolidation, pleural effusion,
or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:  Apparent enlargement of the right cardiac border may be related
to the technique of the study or due to pericardial effusion.  Dedicated PA
and lateral radiographs of the chest at maximal inspiratory effort are
recommended for further evaluation. If the banormality persists, evaluation
with echocardiography is suggested.

PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  IV access needed for antibiotics.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___, the attending
radiologist who was not present but reviewed the case.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right brachial
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was then placed over a
guidewire and a single-lumen PICC line measuring 37 cm in length was then
placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the SVC under
fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided 4 ___
single-lumen PICC line placement via the right brachial venous approach. Final
internal length is 37 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  The line is ready
to use.
